# Gateway vs Direct Integration Trade-offs

Dimension covering the trade-offs of using an LLM gateway versus direct provider
API integration. See [citations.md](../citations.md) for source details.

## Latency Overhead

| Gateway | Overhead | Conditions | Source |
|---------|----------|------------|--------|
| Bifrost | 11µs | 5,000 RPS | [22] |
| Portkey (OSS) | <1ms | Gateway footprint 122kb | [11] |
| LiteLLM | 8ms P95 | 1,000 RPS | [75] |
| Helicone | 8ms P50 | General use | [59] |
| Portkey (managed) | 20-40ms | With guardrails + tracing | [73] |
| Cloudflare AI Gateway | 10-50ms | Edge-based | [73] |

General consensus: purpose-built LLM gateways add 2-20ms overhead [73].
Self-hosting can eliminate 100-400ms network overhead compared to managed
services [73].

## Failure Modes

**Provider downtime is the primary failure mode.** December 2025 data [40]:
- OpenAI: 22 incidents (182.7 total hours, 498 min avg resolution)
- Anthropic: 20 incidents (184.5 total hours, 553 min avg resolution)
- Google Gemini: 0 incidents

Single-provider dependency creates catastrophic failure: the entire application
stalls [41]. With gateway failover, Assembled reported <0.001% request failure
rate during a multi-hour provider outage [41].

**Gateway-introduced failure modes:**
- Streaming timeouts: API Gateway WebSocket has 29-second timeout; REST streaming
  supports up to 15 minutes [73]
- API version mismatches: gateways must forward provider-specific headers
  (anthropic-beta, anthropic-version); failure to forward reduces functionality [16]
- Configuration errors: incorrect provider prefixes, environment variable
  mismatches [14]

**Only 6.15% of LLM incident reports include postmortems** [79], making it
difficult to learn from most incidents.

## Vendor Lock-in

**Migration costs average $315,000 per project** [24]. Lock-in spreads beyond
API calls into fine-tuning paths, conversation histories, embeddings, and
provider-specific features [24]. Agentic workflows increase switching
difficulty [25].

**How gateways help:** Unified API means swapping providers is often a one-line
base URL change [26]. OpenAI-compatible gateways (LiteLLM, Portkey, OpenRouter)
use the same request/response format [14][8][2].

**Market trend:** Gartner predicts 70% of organizations building multi-LLM apps
will use an AI gateway by 2028, up from <5% in 2024 [26]. Currently 40% of
teams use multiple LLM providers [73].

**Gateway lock-in risk:** Gateways themselves can become a lock-in vector.
Evaluation criteria should include "can you leave later" [74]. Self-hosted
gateways with OSS licenses (LiteLLM, Portkey, Bifrost) mitigate this risk.

## Cost Transparency

**Gateway markups:**
- OpenRouter: 5.5% credit fee [2], 5% BYOK fee [2]
- Portkey: $0–$49/month + per-log overage [9]
- LiteLLM (OSS): Free but hidden costs — TCO $2,280–$2,680/month including
  $250 licensing, $300–$700 infrastructure, $1,730 DevOps time [27]
- Some gateways add 20-30% markups bundled to obscure actual cost [65]

**Hidden costs:** Embeddings, retries, logging, rate-limit management add
20-40% of total LLM operational expenses [65].

**Cost tracking benefits:** Gateways provide real-time dashboards across all
providers, per-request cost logging, and budget limits per team/project [66].
LiteLLM tracks costs per virtual key, user, and team [66].

## Developer Experience

**Unified API advantages [20][21]:**
- Keep existing OpenAI SDK code — just change base URL
- Single dashboard replacing separate provider billing portals
- Standardized observability: every request same fidelity, format, zero code changes [77]

**Direct API advantages [28]:**
- Fewer layers to debug
- No abstraction learning curve
- Immediate access to bleeding-edge provider features
- Preferable for small projects with limited scope/risk

**Real-world experience:** A developer managing the Cumbersome iOS/Mac AI client
switched everything to OpenRouter: "5.5% fee worth it for zero data retention,
spending limits, API standardization" [20]. Key benefit: per-key spending limits
capped damage from a Make.com loop bug that consumed $247 in GPT-4 tokens
overnight with direct API (no warning, no kill switch) [20].

**Enterprise case study — Uber [21]:** Built a centralized GenAI Gateway serving
60+ use cases across the company. Drivers: PII redaction, cost attribution per
team, eliminating "disparate integration strategies adopted by different teams."

## Gaps and Limitations

- Limited independent benchmarks comparing gateway latency (most are vendor-published)
- No detailed case studies of migrating FROM a gateway back to direct APIs
- Feature parity lag (time for gateways to support new provider features) is not
  quantified
- Streaming-specific latency benchmarks are scarce
